surface_mechanism_description: The presence of acac-ligands on the surface was shown by the DRIFTS study. The intensity of the stretching vibration of the silica hydroxyl group decreased compared to pure silica. This indicated an exchange reaction between SiO2 OH-groups and the acac-ligands of the precursor. After the calcination step the intensity of n(Si-OH) increased, and the spectra resembled that of a naked support. The traces of the vibrations of cobalt hydroxide, oxide and silicate were seen as the number of ALE cycles increased. Considering the DRIFTS measurements and the C to Co ratio of the uncalcined samples the Co(acac)3 precursor has been proposed to lose one acac-ligand and attach to the silica as Si±O±Co(acac)2. The calcination of this group could easily form CoOx±SiO2 species (calcined catalyst).
